requirement_text.REQ-365: Per explicit user decision: platform-level help (shared screens like login-routing that no tenant owns) is authored through the BA-agent/REQ-ANALYST pipeline, matching the exact platform-vs-tenant split already established for UAT scenarios (REQ-358's scope field, REQ-359's BA-persona/REQ-ANALYST split, REQ-360's login-routing scenario as the worked platform example). This requirement is the authoring-path equivalent for help content: it does not re-derive that split, it applies it. . SCOPE: wherever REQ-363's design placed platform-scope help content (a dedicated table/schema, per that requirement's own acceptance criterion), this requirement adds the write path/tooling REQ-ANALYST (or, once REQ-359 lands, whichever role it specifies for platform content) actually uses to author it — this could be as simple as a direct context-module call analogous to REQ-364's tenant-scoped one, scoped to the platform table instead, reusing REQ-364's create/update/publish/reconfirm shape rather than inventing a parallel one. Explicitly NOT a new UI — platform help authoring is agent-pipeline-driven, matching how platform-scope UAT scenarios are authored (a file/record written by an agent, not a form filled by a human). . FIRST REAL CONTENT: author help for the login-routing screen (the same screen REQ-360's UAT scenario covers) as this requirement's own worked, real example — proves the authoring path end-to-end rather than shipping an authoring mechanism with zero real content using it.

result.summary: Independently read test/specs/REQ-365.md and test/letflow/help/platform_test.exs (and, to verify factual claims made in both, lib/letflow/help/platform.ex and lib/letflow/help/platform_help_content.ex). All five checks pass. (a) Every acceptance criterion has runnable coverage: AC2 (sanitization parity) is covered by create_draft/1's four negative tests plus one positive control, and update_draft/2's HTML-rejection test, all exercising PlatformHelpContent.validate_common/1 -> MarkdownSafety.validate/2 from the platform call site specifically (confirmed MarkdownSafety.validate/2 exists and is called from platform_help_content.ex:98-99). AC3 has one describe block per Letflow.Help.Platform function (create_draft/1, update_draft/2, publish/1, reconfirm/1, withdraw/1, get_by_screen/1), each with positive-path, negative-path, and not-found/not-a-draft/not-live tests, verified against the actual module (e.g. reject_key/4, reject_process_definition_id/1, ensure_draft/1, ensure_live/1, fetch/1 all present and match what the tests assert). AC1 is explicitly and correctly scoped as a structural/design-review property already gated by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/REVIEWER, not re-asserted as its own test -- reasonable, since AC3's function-by-function tests are what would actually catch a runtime deviation from that shape. AC4 is explicitly not duplicated, deferring to the pre-existing, unmodified test/letflow/help_test.exs which TEST-RUNNER runs in the same pass -- a real deferral with a stated mechanism, not a gap. No test is vacuous: the 'allows the design's own safe markdown subset' positive control specifically guards against the negative sanitization tests being trivially true. (b) No 'TODO'/'@tag :skip' found in either file (grepped both). (c) All fixtures use unique_screen_id/1 (System.unique_integer/1-suffixed) per test -- no shared/hardcoded screen_id, confirmed by reading every test; the two-row get_by_screen/1 test uses two independently-generated screen_ids. (d) Tests are self-sufficient: every test calls create_draft!/1 (or draft_attrs/1) itself rather than relying on another test's data, and Letflow.DataCase's sandboxed transaction (async: false) rolls back after each test, so there is no cross-test pollution despite platform_help_content being a single shared (non-tenant-scoped) table. (e) No hardcoded secrets/connection strings found (grepped for password/secret/postgres:///api_key/token= in both files -- no matches).
